title: An AWS Key Was Pushed to a Public Repository
intro: GitHub's secret scanning just emailed: an AWS access key was found in commit 8c9d0e1 of a public repo. It was pushed 20 minutes ago. Bots scan public repos for exactly this within minutes.

steps.prompt: First priority: kill the key before anything else. Deactivate it in AWS (key id AKIAEXAMPLE1234).
expected_commands: aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE1234 --status Inactive --user-name ci-deploy
steps.hint: Cleaning git history comes later. A live leaked key is the emergency.

steps.prompt: Check whether the key was used by anyone other than you in the last hour.
steps.fake_output:
EventName: RunInstances   SourceIP: 185.220.x.x  EventTime: 12:41:07
EventName: RunInstances   SourceIP: 185.220.x.x  EventTime: 12:41:09
(12 events from an unknown IP)
steps.hint: CloudTrail records every API call made with the key.

steps.prompt: Someone launched instances with it — likely crypto miners. List running instances to find them.
steps.fake_output:
i-0evil1  p3.16xlarge  us-east-1  launched 12:41
i-0evil2  p3.16xlarge  us-east-1  launched 12:41
(10 more)
steps.hint: Look for instance types and launch times that don't match anything your team runs.

steps.prompt: Find which files in the offending commit contained the key.
Store a new, properly-scoped credential as a CI secret (never in the repo).
steps.fake_output: ✓ Set Actions secret AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY for acme/tools
steps.hint: Better still: replace static keys with OIDC so there's nothing long-lived to leak.

resolution: Order of operations is everything in a leaked-credential incident: revoke first, investigate second, clean up third. Within 20 minutes of the push, an attacker had already used the key to launch a dozen expensive GPU instances for crypto mining — typical for keys leaked in public repos. Terminating those instances and reviewing every CloudTrail event from that key is mandatory; the attacker may also have created new IAM users or keys for persistence. Rewriting git history afterwards (git filter-repo, BFG) is only hygiene — forks and caches keep the old commit, so a leaked secret must always be treated as permanently public. Prevention: pre-commit secret scanning (gitleaks), GitHub push protection, and OIDC-based short-lived credentials so there is no static key to leak in the first place.
